routes.name: Black Sea grain to Athens, escorted by triremes
routes.goods_source: general history; not from a cargo manifest
routes.citation: Alfonso Moreno, Feeding the Democracy: The Athenian Grain Supply in the Fifth and Fourth Centuries BC (Oxford, 2007); Lionel Casson, Ships and Seamanship in the Ancient World (Princeton, 1971).
routes.notes: Kerch Strait (Panticapaeum) through the Bosporus and the Hellespont to Piraeus. The ship marker is a trireme because Athenian warships escorted the grain convoys; most grain sailed in merchant hulls. Dates and route from general history; check against the cited work before publishing.
citations: Alfonso Moreno, Feeding the Democracy: The Athenian Grain Supply in the Fifth and Fourth Centuries BC (Oxford, 2007); Lionel Casson, Ships and Seamanship in the Ancient World (Princeton, 1971).

routes.name: Roman grain fleet, Alexandria to Ostia
routes.goods_source: general history; not from a cargo manifest
routes.citation: Lionel Casson, Ships and Seamanship in the Ancient World (Princeton, 1971); Geoffrey Rickman, The Corn Supply of Ancient Rome (Oxford, 1980).
routes.notes: The long northabout passage of the grain ships: Alexandria to Lycia, Rhodes, south of Crete, Malta, the Strait of Messina and up to Ostia. Dates and route from general history; check against the cited work before publishing.
citations: Lionel Casson, Ships and Seamanship in the Ancient World (Princeton, 1971); Geoffrey Rickman, The Corn Supply of Ancient Rome (Oxford, 1980).

routes.name: Red Sea to Muziris on the monsoon
routes.goods_source: general history; not from a cargo manifest
routes.citation: Lionel Casson (ed. and trans.), The Periplus Maris Erythraei (Princeton, 1989).
routes.notes: Berenike down the Red Sea and across the Arabian Sea to the Malabar coast with the southwest monsoon. Dates and route from general history; check against the cited work before publishing.
citations: Lionel Casson (ed. and trans.), The Periplus Maris Erythraei (Princeton, 1989).
